methodology: A facile and efficient new strategy for the synthesis of hydrophilic quantum dot (QD)-labeled fluorescent molecularly imprinted polymer microspheres was developed through one-step grafting of a red CdTe QD-labeled 2,4-D-MIP layer with hydrophilic polyethylene glycol brushes onto preformed uniform 'living' polymer microspheres via one-pot surface-initiated activator regenerated by electron transfer (ARGET) atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) (SI-ARGET ATRP).
research_objective: The objective was to develop a highly useful optosensor with high 2,4-D selectivity and sensitivity for detecting the widely used herbicide 2,4-D in undiluted vegetable juices.

key_findings.finding: The use of SI-ARGET ATRP significantly reduced the applied copper catalyst concentration, alleviating the quenching effect of the copper catalyst on the fluorescence of the QD-labeled MIP.
The developed hydrophilic red CdTe QD (rQD)-labeled MIP microspheres can directly and selectively optosensing 2,4-D in the undiluted vegetable complex sample.
The use of ARGET ATRP can significantly reduce the copper catalyst concentration in the MIPs capable of directly and selectively optosensing herbicides and pesticides.
The hydrophilic fluorescent 2,4-D-MIP microspheres with surface-grafted PEG brushes significantly enhanced their surface hydrophilicity and led to largely reduced nonspecific template binding.

properties.context: Tg (glass transition temperature) was discussed in the context of polymer properties but not measured or quantified.

properties.value: ratiometric MIP-based microfluidic paper chip for optosensing 2,4-D in cucumber juice
properties.context: obtained ratiometric fluorescent MIP particles with balanced dual D
Surface roughness (Ra) of the polymer microspheres was discussed in relation to their performance, but specific values were not provided.
